title: ATTITUDE HEADING REFERENCE SYSTEM (AHRS) - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
question: What precautions should be taken during the reinstallation of the GRS-77 AHRS to prevent incorrect information and ensure proper calibration?
answer: CAUTION: Do not move the unit mounting racks if the GRS-77 AHRS is removed and replaced after post-installation calibration has been completed. The AHRS can give incorrect information.Remove the AHRS unit . (1) Make sure the MASTER and AVIONICS switches are in the off position. (2) Remove the tailcone access/inspection plate  to get access to the NAV/COM units. Refer to Chapter 6, Access/Inspection Plates - Description and Operation. (3) Disconnect the electrical connector . (4)  Remove the screws that attach the AHRS unit to the mounting tray. (5)  Remove the AHRS unit from the airplane.Install the AHRS unit . Put the AHRS unit in position in the mounting tray and attach to the tray with screws. (a) If the fasteners that attach the mounting racks are loosened for any reason, the post-installation calibration must be completed. Refer to the Garmin GRS 77/GMU 44 (2) Connect the electrical connector . (3) Install the tailcone access/inspection plate . Refer to Chapter 6, Access/Inspection Do a check to make sure the AHRS operates correctly. Refer to the Garmin G1000 Line

title: ATTITUDE HEADING REFERENCE SYSTEM (AHRS) - MAINTENANCE PRACTICES
